Run a SQL query against a document

Source: R/sql.R
grist_sql.Rd

grist_sql() runs a read-only SELECT query against the SQLite database behind a Grist document. grist_count() counts the rows in a table.

Usage

grist_sql(doc, query, args = NULL, timeout = NULL, convert = c("basic", "raw"))

grist_count(doc, table)

Arguments

doc

A grist_doc object, document ID or document URL. See grist_doc().

query

A single SQL SELECT statement without a trailing semicolon. Use ? placeholders for values in args.

args

A list or vector of values for the ? placeholders in query.

timeout

Query timeout in milliseconds. The server's default (1000) can only be reduced.

convert

How to convert returned values: "basic" simplifies JSON values into vectors, and "raw" returns list-columns of the values exactly as the API does. SQL results carry no column types, so dates are returned as numbers.

table

Table ID, as listed by grist_tables().

Value

grist_sql() returns a data frame. grist_count() returns the number of rows as an integer.

See also

Other records: grist_records(), grist_resolve_refs()

Examples

if (FALSE) {
doc <- grist_doc("am2iHJ9Amvo7Ve3EE5emtu")
grist_sql(doc, "SELECT * FROM Pets WHERE popularity >= ?", args = 50)
grist_count(doc, "Pets")
}
